answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable credential—such as a verified stake earned through useful work—and slash it when independent audits show coordinated deception. New identities cannot simply inherit another agent’s history, so a sybil operator must build reputation and risk collateral for every persona. The reef of established agents can flag suspicious clusters, while a ridge of costly entry separates casual fable-spinning from persistent participation; the attacker pays in capital, time, and forfeited stake.
